Scikit-learn’s default tokenizer splits hyphenated identifiers. Recommended explicit configuration: `TfidfVectorizer(analyzer='word', token_pattern=r'(?u)\b\w+(?:-\w+)*\b', lowercase=True, strip_accents=None, stop_words=None, ngram_range=(1,1), min_df=1, max_df=1.0, max_features=None, binary=False, norm='l2', use_idf=True, smooth_idf=True, sublinear_tf=False, dtype=np.float64)`. This preserves ASCII-hyphen identifiers such as `WH-1000XM5` as single tokens, including single-character components; explicitly normalize Unicode dash variants if required. Freeze the fitted vocabulary, IDF, item-ID mapping and package versions. L2-normalized TF-IDF makes dot products equal cosine similarities. [Vectorizer documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/1.5/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html).

For exact neighbors with bounded intermediate storage, recommended implementation: keep TF-IDF sparse, multiply query blocks against catalog blocks, immediately retain each query’s best k candidates, then merge using the same ordering. Bound both block dimensions: sparse products can become dense. Storage includes input matrices, multiplication workspace, block results and retained neighbors; `working_memory` in scikit-learn targets distance chunks, not total process memory. Never materialize the full catalog-by-catalog matrix. [SciPy dot](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.sparse.csr_matrix.dot.html), [chunking documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.pairwise_distances_chunked.html).

Define ranking as descending similarity, then ascending item ID: `np.lexsort((item_ids, -scores))[:k]`. Apply exclusions before selection. Plain `argpartition` followed by sorting can discard preferred IDs tied at the cutoff; resolve all boundary ties explicitly. Include implicit zero similarities when fewer than k positive matches remain, including empty-title rows. Fixed arithmetic settings support reproducibility; ID ordering resolves exact ties, not floating-point differences across environments. [lexsort](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.lexsort.html), [argpartition](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.argpartition.html).
